notes: The partition-based rules preserve the existing implementation’s behavior for all plain string inputs, including whitespace, malformed lines, and quote handling. The helper extraction, public exports, and unchanged tests can all be satisfied within kvparse/**.
rule: a conflict is demonstrated only when it names existing criteria and its witness program, run on the unmodified repository in a disposable sandbox branch, prints a line starting with 'CONTRADICTION' that names at least one of them and exits with code 3; it is GROUNDED, and may end the run as infeasible, only when every named requirement is an authoritative task criterion (TC) and the witness is constrained (no function, class, lambda or dynamic type, no dynamic code; values of the input domain and the unchanged code only); a demonstrated conflict that involves a derived criterion (AC) or an unconstrained witness is held for a human; a claimed-only conflict never ends a run; the witness's reasoning is the model's and its execution is recorded, which is not a formal proof of impossibility
input_domain: the input domain of a witness is the set of values the task names or implies: literals of the built-in types the task's statement and criteria use (plain str, int, list, dict, bytes, None and so on) and values computed from them by the unchanged repository code; instances of subclasses of built-in types, objects with overridden special methods and other adversarial values are OUTSIDE the domain unless the task names them explicitly
